What happened

Field staff reported that the separator was overfilling and the dump valve was not opening. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0121-0008 showed the wellhead at 15.0 °C with the air at 10.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Root cause

Controller float and switch failure.

Safety and permits

  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

Work done

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0121-012

Asset: WELL-0121 (NE-07 Well 121, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 21 Jan 2024 08:00 · Finished: 31 Jan 2024 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 250 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0121-0066 on 2024-01-18 Report written: 01 Feb 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0121-0066 showed the wellhead at 13.7 °C with the air at 7.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0121-035

Asset: WELL-0121 (NE-07 Well 121, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 09 Oct 2026 08:00 · Planned finish: 28 Oct 2026 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 462 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0121-0205 on 2026-10-08 Report written: 16 Oct 2026 · Status: interim report, work still in progress

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0121-0205 showed the wellhead at 29.0 °C with the air at 25.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well is expected to stay shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain is making the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done so far

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.

Still to do: complete the remaining repair steps, test the equipment and return the well to production.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Not done yet. The work is expected to finish on 28 Oct 2026; testing and return to service will be recorded in the final report.

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.
  • Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).
